trial_name: APROCCHSS — Hydrocortisone plus Fludrocortisone for Adults with Septic Shock (2018)
citation: Annane D, Renault A, Brun-Buisson C, et al. Hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone for adults with septic shock. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(9):809-818.
trial_type: RCT — multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2x2 factorial (later two-group)
one_liner: In adults with persistent septic shock, 7 days of hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone significantly reduced 90-day all-cause mortality and accelerated shock recovery.

pico.population: Adult ICU patients with persistent septic shock within 24 hours of onset requiring vasopressors despite fluid resuscitation.
pico.intervention: Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate 50 mg IV q6h (200 mg/day) plus fludrocortisone 50 mcg enteral daily for 7 days.
pico.comparison: Matched IV placebo q6h plus matched enteral placebo tablets daily for 7 days.
pico.outcome: 90-day all-cause mortality (primary); ICU, hospital, 28-day, and 180-day mortality; vasopressor-free and organ-failure-free days; safety endpoints.

background.existing_knowledge: Septic shock remains a leading cause of ICU mortality. Low-dose corticosteroids were hypothesized to accelerate shock reversal, but trial results were conflicting.
background.knowledge_gap: Divergent findings between earlier corticosteroid trials left uncertainty regarding mortality benefit, patient targeting, and the role of mineralocorticoid co-administration.
background.hypothesis: In adults with persistent septic shock, adjunctive low-dose hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone reduces all-cause 90-day mortality and hastens resolution of cardiovascular and organ failure.

methods.design: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT in 34 French ICUs (CRICS-TRIGGERSEP Network). Initially a 2x2 factorial trial evaluating drotrecogin alfa (activated), continued as a two-group corticosteroid trial after drotrecogin alfa was withdrawn from the market.

inclusion: Adult ICU patients with suspected or confirmed infection
Persistent septic shock requiring vasopressors despite fluid resuscitation
Randomisation within 24 hours of shock onset
High baseline severity (SAPS II mean ~56 ± 19, ~92% mechanically ventilated, ~27–28% receiving renal-replacement therapy)
exclusion: Vasopressor therapy >24 hours prior to screening/randomisation
Protocol-defined conditions limiting safety/feasibility (including bleeding contraindications during original factorial phase)

methods.intervention: Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate 50 mg IV every 6 hours (200 mg/day) for 7 days PLUS fludrocortisone 50 mcg once daily (oral or nasogastric) for 7 days.
methods.comparison: Matched IV placebo injections every 6 hours PLUS matched oral/nasogastric placebo tablets once daily for 7 days.
methods.blinding: Double-blind (patients, clinicians, investigators, outcome assessors); matched placebo preparations.
methods.sample_size_power: 1280 patients planned to detect a 10% absolute reduction in 90-day mortality (45% to 35%) with 95% power at two-sided alpha=0.05. Enrolled 1241 (97% of target) when drug expiry was reached.
secondary_outcomes: All-cause mortality at day 28, ICU discharge, hospital discharge, and day 180
Decision to withhold or withdraw active treatment by day 90
methods.follow_up: 180 days (6 months) for mortality and safety endpoints.

headline_bullets: Hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone reduced 90-day all-cause mortality (43.0% vs 49.1%; RR 0.88; P=0.03).
Mortality reductions were directionally consistent at ICU discharge, hospital discharge, and 180 days.
Treatment significantly accelerated hemodynamic recovery (vasopressor-free days 17.8 vs 15.0; P<0.001) and increased organ-failure–free days.
Hyperglycemia was more frequent with steroids, but no increases in gastroduodenal bleeding or superinfections were observed.

outcomes_table.note: Primary comparison after trial continued as two-group corticosteroid trial
Numerical reduction; not statistically significant at 5% level

outcomes_table.outcome: Decision to withhold/withdraw treatment by day 90

outcomes_table.note: Values are Mean ± SD; indicates faster shock reversal
Values are Mean ± SD; non-significant trend
Values are Mean ± SD; composite recovery metric
No excess GI bleeding signal with steroids

safety: Increased days with blood glucose ≥150 mg/dL: 4.3 ± 4.1 vs 3.4 ± 3.8 days (P<0.001).
Gastroduodenal bleeding by day 28: 6.4% vs 7.2% (RR 0.88; 95% CI 0.58–1.34; P=0.56).
Neurologic sequelae (MDRS >1) by day 180: 24.9% vs 20.8% (RR 1.20; 95% CI 0.98–1.47; P=0.08).

domains.notes: Central randomisation with permuted blocks (size 8) and stratification by ICU. Concealment maintained via identical placebos.
Double-blind design with matched IV and oral placebos. Primary outcome is objective all-cause mortality.
Primary analysis was intention-to-treat without missing data imputation. Small loss to follow-up at 180 days (611/614 and 625/627).
Clear biological separation demonstrated by metabolic effects (glucose ≥150 mg/dL: 4.3 vs 3.4 days; P<0.001) and vasopressor-free days (17.8 vs 15.0; P<0.001).
Well-balanced groups: SAPS II ~56, mechanical ventilation ~92%, RRT ~27–28%, baseline norepinephrine-equivalent dose ~1.02 vs 1.14 mcg/kg/min.

internal_validity.verdict: Internal validity is strong for the primary mortality endpoint due to concealed randomisation, double-blinding, and objective outcome assessment, with moderate caution required for secondary outcomes given design evolution and lack of multiplicity adjustment.

domains.notes: Severely ill adult ICU population with high vasopressor requirements and mechanical ventilation (~92%) in high-income country ICUs.
Conducted across 34 French ICUs. Dosing is highly pragmatic, but fludrocortisone requires enteral access and availability.

external_validity.verdict: Generalisability is high to adult ICU patients with vasopressor-dependent septic shock in high-resource settings, but less clear in lower-acuity sepsis or settings lacking enteral drug delivery.

strengths: Large, multicenter, double-blind, randomized controlled design
Extended follow-up to 180 days with minimal attrition
High baseline illness severity representative of clinical septic shock
limitations: Complex trial history including discontinuation of drotrecogin alfa factorial arm and recruitment interruptions
Stopped slightly short of target sample size due to drug expiration (1241/1280 enrolled, 97%)
Multiple secondary outcomes reported without multiplicity adjustment
Cannot isolate the relative contribution of fludrocortisone vs hydrocortisone alone

critical_appraisal.summary: APROCCHSS is a high-quality RCT demonstrating that hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone reduces 90-day mortality and hastens shock recovery in severe septic shock.
strengths: Double-blind placebo control with excellent allocation concealment
High protocol adherence and robust ITT analysis
weaknesses: Inability to differentiate independent effects of hydrocortisone vs fludrocortisone
Factorial design disruption during trial execution

sections.authors_conclusion: Adjunctive therapy with hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone for 7 days significantly reduced 90-day all-cause mortality and ICU mortality among patients with septic shock.

clinical_bottom_line.verdict: Supports routine administration of low-dose hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone in patients with septic shock requiring ongoing vasopressor therapy despite fluid resuscitation.
clinical_bottom_line.applies_to: Adult ICU patients with severe, vasopressor-dependent septic shock within 24 hours of onset.
clinical_bottom_line.does_not_mean: Does not justify high-dose or short-duration steroid bursts, nor steroid use in mild sepsis without shock.
implementation_caveats: Fludrocortisone 50 mcg requires enteral access (oral or NG tube).
Requires close blood glucose monitoring due to an increased risk of hyperglycemia.
Treatment should be initiated early (within 24 hours of shock onset).

controversies.topic: Trial design evolution and factorial termination
controversies.notes: Transition from a 2x2 factorial trial (with drotrecogin alfa) to a two-arm trial and enrolment suspensions complicated execution, though randomised comparison remained valid.

controversies.topic: Discordance with ADRENAL and CORTICUS trials
controversies.notes: APROCCHSS showed 90-day mortality reduction with hydrocortisone + fludrocortisone, whereas ADRENAL (hydrocortisone continuous infusion alone) and CORTICUS (hydrocortisone boluses alone) did not show mortality reduction.

Because hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone were given together, APROCCHSS cannot prove whether mineralocorticoid addition is required or if hydrocortisone dosing/bolus strategy accounts for the benefit.

context_related_trials.relation: Evaluated continuous hydrocortisone infusion alone (200 mg/day) in septic shock; found faster shock reversal and fewer ICU days, but no difference in 90-day mortality.
Evaluated hydrocortisone boluses in septic shock; found faster shock reversal but no mortality benefit and raised concerns about secondary infections.
Analyzed IV hydrocortisone without routine mineralocorticoid; found no mortality reduction, but increased vasopressor-free days (mean diff 1.24 days; 95% CI 0.74–1.73).
Showed hydrocortisone + fludrocortisone reduced mortality vs placebo (RR 0.85; 95% CrI 0.72–0.99), with non-definitive difference vs hydrocortisone alone (RR 0.88; 95% CrI 0.74–1.03).
Issues conditional recommendation for corticosteroids in vasopressor-dependent septic shock (hydrocortisone 200 mg/day), recommending against high-dose short-duration regimens.
Concluded corticosteroids probably reduce short- and long-term mortality in sepsis overall.

unresolved_questions: Is mineralocorticoid (fludrocortisone) co-administration strictly necessary, or is hydrocortisone monotherapy equivalent?
Does bolus hydrocortisone administration differ clinically from continuous infusion?
Are specific infection phenotypes (e.g., community-acquired pneumonia) differentially responsive to combination corticosteroids?

numbers_to_remember: Dose: Hydrocortisone 50 mg IV q6h + Fludrocortisone 50 mcg enteral daily for 7 days
quick_recall.one_line_takeaway: In vasopressor-dependent septic shock, adding 7 days of hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone reduces 90-day mortality and accelerates shock reversal.
